solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tennis champ once taking drink without cake, oddly

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drink wraps round the other letters

parts.note: beer is a common drink

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first and third letters of the word cake

explanation.surface: A former tennis star having a drink but skipping the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'oddly' picks the odd letters of 'cake'.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Becker, the German player, won Wimbledon three times and is now retired, hence 'once'.

clue.text: One writing about a poet from Spanish island

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pen's letters go round the rest

parts.note: a Bic is a ballpoint pen, a thing that writes
Edward Lear, the nonsense poet

explanation.surface: A writer composing verse about a poet from a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One writing' looks like a person but is a pen brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for the Mediterranean archipelago of Majorca, Minorca and Ibiza, belonging to Spain.

clue.text: Members of royal family, Conservative types

parts.note: sorts are kinds or types

explanation.surface: Royals described as conservative kinds of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is the spouse of a reigning monarch, such as a queen's husband, and so part of the royal family.

clue.text: Group of Cambridge lecturers ready to take charge

indicators.note: a group of letters is taken from inside the words Cambridge lecturers, running across the word break

explanation.surface: A body of Cambridge dons poised to assume control.
explanation.definitionFit: Elect after a title, as in president-elect, means chosen and about to take office.

clue.text: Say nothing during Disney film with unspeakable acting

indicators.note: during means inside the length of, so one piece sits within the film title

parts.note: Dumbo is the Disney film about a flying elephant
SH is the command to keep quiet

explanation.surface: Instruction to stay silent while watching a Disney film with poor acting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dumb show is a performance in mime, acting with no spoken words.

clue.text: Most cruel guy, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of Most cruel guy may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Speculation about who the cruellest man might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly customer is an unpleasant, dangerous person, which a very cruel man may well be.

clue.text: Type of carpet — American woman has metre laid around small room

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman
loo is British slang for a toilet, a small room

explanation.surface: An American woman fitting carpet around a small room by the metre.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadloom is carpet woven in wide widths on a broad loom, used for fitted carpeting.

clue.text: Asian island supplying hot, top quality bread

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
A1 means first-rate; the 1 is read as the letter I
naan or nan is a South Asian flatbread

explanation.surface: An Asian island that supplies hot, first-class bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Hainan is a large island province in the south of China.

clue.text: Rebuked for wearing hairpiece

definitions.meaning: to give someone a wigging is to scold them

explanation.surface: Someone told off for wearing a toupee.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigging is British slang for a telling-off; the other sense is simply having a wig on.

clue.text: Don't go hiding among gunslingers

indicators.note: the letters are concealed inside the word gunslingers

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay put, concealed among armed cowboys.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to stay on and delay leaving, the opposite of going.

clue.text: Flipping out

definitions.meaning: a mild British intensifier, a euphemism for a stronger swear word
flowers that are out are in flower

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are mild British expletives and plants in flower; flipping and blooming are interchangeable minced oaths.

clue.text: Device used by some writers is nothing but repetition

parts.note: all as in it's all talk, meaning nothing but
iteration is repeating something

explanation.surface: A literary technique dismissed as mere repetition.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating initial sounds in neighbouring words is a stylistic technique used by poets and writers.

clue.text: Following leader, having a job attached to police centre

parts.note: a post is a position or job

indicators.note: centre asks for the middle letters of police, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: A follower of the chief taking a post attached to police headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostolic means relating to the apostles, the followers of Christ, or to the Pope as their successor.

clue.text: Bird given diamonds by ladies' man

parts.note: D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds
a rake is a womaniser

explanation.surface: A girl receiving diamonds from a womaniser, 'bird' being slang for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' suggests British slang for a girlfriend, fitting the surface; it is the feathered sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A drake is a male duck, a kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: During days at school, is din endless about break time?

parts.note: in means during, as in in the summer
term is the period of school days

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the shortened word is read backwards
endless means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a din is a noise

explanation.surface: Asking whether a noisy school day is ending in a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts NOISE to NOIS, and 'about' turns it to SION.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermission is an interval or pause, a break in proceedings.

clue.text: Another chance to see film about soldiers on fields close to Passchendaele

parts.note: re means about or concerning
RE is the Royal Engineers, the British Army corps
leas are meadows or fields

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of Passchendaele

explanation.surface: A war film about soldiers in the fields near Passchendaele, the First World War battle, back in cinemas.
explanation.definitionFit: A rerelease is a film put out again in cinemas, giving audiences a second showing.

clue.text: Conservative's regret pound has gone up in 24 hours

indicators.note: in places the inner pieces within the day's abbreviation

parts.note: Tue is the short form of Tuesday, a day of 24 hours
to rue is to regret

indicators.note: gone up means read upwards, backwards in a down entry

parts.note: lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A Tory politician sorry that sterling rose within a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has gone up' turns LB to BL.
explanation.definitionFit: A true blue is a staunch, loyal supporter of the British Conservative Party, whose colour is blue.

clue.text: Nationalised express travel

parts.note: to state is to express in words
to run is to travel, as a bus runs

explanation.surface: A nationalised railway's express service.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationalised industry is owned and operated by the government.

clue.text: Honour former editor in review

indicators.note: under review, the letters of former editor are revised into a new order

explanation.surface: A past editor being honoured in a critical review.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of Merit is a British order awarded by the monarch, a high personal distinction.

clue.text: Politician overwhelmed by endless corruption is to get out

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: decay is rot or corruption
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician engulfed by endless sleaze is set to quit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final letter of the synonym for corruption; in a down entry 'overwhelmed by' means placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly.

clue.text: Begin to like second piece of filming, say

indicators.note: say means the words are spoken and heard as something else

parts.note: take two is the second shot of a scene in film-making

explanation.surface: Warming to the second shot in a film shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow fond of someone or something; an idiom for starting to like.

clue.text: Message with misinformation, circulated about mother

indicators.note: about means surrounding the other piece
circulated means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lie is false information
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A misleading message forwarded around about someone's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' turns LIE to EIL, which goes 'about' MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is a message sent between computers.

clue.text: Repair men in a small town taking little change

indicators.note: in places the repair and the men within the outer letters

parts.note: T is an abbreviation for town
to mend is to repair

explanation.surface: Repairmen in a small town making a minor change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair men' looks like one word but gives MEND and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a small alteration, especially to a text or law.

clue.text: Lawman for the stars

definitions.meaning: the Athenian legislator famous for harsh laws

explanation.surface: A sheriff for Hollywood celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek lawgiver gave us 'draconian'; the same name is a constellation of stars.

clue.text: Way mass introduces song — such as this?

definitions.text: Way mass introduces song — such as this?

parts.note: Ave is short for avenue, a way
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
an aria is a solo song in opera

explanation.surface: Musing on a hymn that ushers in the singing at Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduces' places M before ARIA; read whole, the clue describes the prayer set to music.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is a prayer often set to music, famously by Schubert and Gounod, sung at Mass.

clue.text: Unhealthy appearance of friend — gosh

parts.note: a pal is a friend
lor is a dated exclamation of surprise, a form of lord

explanation.surface: Surprise at how ill a friend looks.
explanation.definitionFit: Pallor is an unhealthy paleness of the face.

clue.text: One Sprite, mostly fizzy: just what the body needs

indicators.note: fizzy suggests the letters bubbling into a new order
mostly means the drink's name loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A soft drink advertised as exactly what the body requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts Sprite to SPRIT; 'fizzy' mixes ONE with it.
explanation.definitionFit: These nutrients are essential to the body for building and repairing tissue.

clue.text: Enter, once I'm dressed

indicators.note: dressed means arranged, as troops are dressed into line, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone calling 'enter' once they have put their clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitation to come inside, the usual reply to a knock.
